'''Greg Bole Crush The Rebellion''' is a [[Dark]] constructed list published on Decipher Deck Designs.

== Deck info ==
* '''Player:''' [[Greg Bole]]
* '''Published:''' July 1996 (Decipher Deck Designs)
* '''Format:''' [[Premiere - A New Hope]]
* '''Side:''' [[Dark]]
* '''Starting Card:''' {{CardLink|Tatooine: Lars' Moisture Farm|Premiere-D-tatooinelarsmoisturefarm.gif}}
* '''Strategy:''' Crush The Rebellion
* '''GEMP Importable deck:''' [[Media:PANH Crush The Rebellion Bole DS 1996.txt |Download]]

== Strategy ==

This deck is pretty easy to make because it's just a watered down verion of my "Rule With An Iron Fist" power deck. I took out almost all of the R1s (left in two) and some of the R2s. This is a deck *many* more people can build but it works on all the same principles. The strategy/explaination is largely the same, but I deleted and added where needed for the card changes.

== Strategy ==

'''Introduction:''' This is a very feasible deck for someone to make who doesn't have a ton of money invested in cards. It just goes to show that you can make a strong, competative deck without tons of rares. This deck has only two R1s: Darth Vader and Presense of the Force and only seven R2s. The main theme of this deck is to rule Tatooine with an iron fist on either the land or in space with the possibility for controlling additional systems.

'''Strategy:''' Deploy in force to a Tatooine site, establish an unbeatable presense and force drain each turn. If the sites become too hairy (for whatever reason) the whole operation can easily be taken aboard a Star Destroyer to drain for the same amount at a system. If the opponent dares to deploy 2-4 characters alone, transport your entire strike force with Elis Helrot and hit them for a huge battle loss.

'''Locations:''' The locations were chosen for a number of reasons:

a) High force generation in order to deploy the mains and the ISDs

b) Bonuses to force drain on Tatooine, the starting location allows a force drain of 2 a turn, which should be increased to 3-4 by lightsaber wielding characters.

c) No Death Star sites at all so you don't have to worry about protecting two fronts. The often used DS: War Room was avoided for this reason and because of the text allowing the LS to get an extra battle destiny when attacking there.

'''Characters:'''The characters used can be divided into three main categories

1.High Ability Imperials - Vader, Djas, Prophetess, and Motti all have ability three or higher (much higher in Lord Vader's case!) and can easily wield lightsabers for boosted force drains and to kill the opponents main characters.

2.Imperial Pilots - DS-61-2 adds 3 power to ISDs and can be used as backup on Tatooine. The other pilots add less but supply the much needed ability for destiny draws at systems.

3. Aliens - the infamous team of Dr. Evazan and Ponda Baba would have won the Cantina skirmish if Darth Vader had been there to strike down Obi-Wan. Ponda gets a power bonus with the "good doctor" who in turn can be used to operate on hit opponents to remove them from the battle

'''Starships:''' The Star Destroyers can be used to force drain at systems, shuttle around characters, and add a +1 bonus per ship to battles on Tatooine when you control the system. The Scouts can act as attrition fodder to keep the ISDs flying and have greater range with their higher number hyperdrives.

'''Vehicles:''' The Ubrikkian 9000 can transport three characters almost anywhere on Tatooine to counter force drains and reacts to battles. And the extra two power can really come in handy as well!

'''Weapons and Devices:''' As mentioned before the lightsabers are an integral element of this (and almost any) deck. They provide the ability to drain greater amounts of force and kill your opponents main characters. The comlink is to deploy one character at a second or third force draining site with the ability to rescue him by reacting with even more forces from your hand.

'''Effects:''' Presence Of The Force should be deployed where ever your main force is draining to give you not only +1 to your force drain but also one more force to activate every turn. Just don't let that site fall into Rebel hands. Reactor Terminal is a must to recirculate high destiny cards back into your deck near the end of the game in order to have guaranteed high weapon and battle destiny draws. Another nasty tournament trick is to get almost your entire hand back into your life force the turn before you win to boost up your life force points for your win.

'''Used Interrupts:''' Until they are more balanced Senses and Alters are the name of the game. If you have more than your opponent your Interrupts and Effects work while theirs are canceled. If you win a large "Sense War" (where each of your keep cancelling the others one after another) whoever gets the last one out keeps them all, the loser loses them all...creating a major tactical advantage for the winner. As mentioned before the Elis' are there to transport your hit-squad onto Yavin 4 for a huge invasion or to wipe out a smaller force that's running from you on Tatooine.

'''Lost Interrupts:''' These are either to give you extra battle destiny or add flexibility to your hand. Pound the enemy with a Gravel Storm, block that main character with a Barrier, switch those destiny draws with Takeel, these Interrupts always keep your opponent guessing.

'''Strategy:''' Your strategy for this deck is pretty straight-forward. Rule with an Iron Fist. Keep control over one location draining your opponent for 2-4 force a turn (depending on how many lightsabers you draw and when the Presence of the Force comes out). If they are draining you elsewhere you might have to ready an attack. This can be done easily with Elis Helrot, or be mobilized and supported by a few Imperial Star Destroyers. If you have over 12 power (which shouldn't be hard with Lord Vader out) and a good Interrupt or two up your sleeve, then transport to where the Rebels have dared to deploy and crush them under your heal. However you must be careful of comlinks, CZ-3s, vehicles, and other things that allow your opponent to react to a battle. They could have a desperate, yet cunning, Rebel trick up their sleeves.

'''End-Game:''' After sustaining heavy losses due to your force drains and a major attack or two the Rebel scum will be weakened. If they lose a long Sense War you will have the upper hand to brush aside any Interrupts that might give them an edge. Either continue to slowly tighten your grip on the throat of Tatooine, crushing it's force between your fingers, or swoop in for a final blow that will finish them off. The only real threats to your overwhelming forces would be a) Obi-Wan with a lightsaber b) many extra destiny draws against you through the use of a combination of Interrupts or c) a suprise counterassult by their ability to react to a force drain or attack. Of course you have ways to counter each of these threats:

A. Darth Vader with a lightsaber is a good match for Obi-Wan.

B. If you have Sense superiority you should be able to cancel any particularly nasty Rebel Interrupts. One fantastic part of this deck is with Darth Vader on the table your Senses and Alters can never fail! There are no destiny 6 cards in the deck!

C. You do have to be careful of Rebel reacts, but remember Sense cards can cancel reacts as well as Interrupts!

The strength of this deck is sheer power combined with the ability to shut down Rebel opposition. If you deny your opponent the chance to deploy, use main characters, play Interrupts, and react to your threat, then you have the upper hand and control play. This is not a deck for the weak of heart. It combines raw power and several devious Imperial tricks to "crush their insignificant rebellion".

LONG LIVE THE EMPIRE!
